prompt: Move your king one square toward the center of the board — onto b2.

feedback.default: The king moves exactly one square in any direction, including diagonally. From a1, which single square gets you toward the middle of the board?

successExplanation: Kb2 moves one square diagonally — the king can step in any of the eight directions around it, always just one square at a time.

prompt: Move your king onto the f-file, one rank up.

feedback.default: Read the files left to right: a, b, c, d, e, f... From e1, the f-file is one step to the right. Combine that with moving one rank up.

successExplanation: Kf2 is one square right (onto the f-file) and one square up (onto rank 2) — exactly the kind of single-square step every king move is.

prompt: Slide the rook straight up the d-file to the top of the board.

feedback.default: The rook moves in straight lines only — up/down a file or left/right along a rank, any distance. From d3, which square is at the very top of the d-file?

successExplanation: Rd8 slides straight up the d-file all the way to the last rank — exactly how a rook moves: straight lines, any distance, until something blocks it.

prompt: Capture the pawn blocking your rook's path up the file.

feedback.default: The rook can't jump over the pawn on d4 — but it can capture it. Which move lands your rook right on top of that pawn?

successExplanation: Rxd4 captures the blocking pawn — a rook stops at the first piece in its path, but if that piece is an enemy, it can capture it there.

prompt: Move the bishop along its diagonal as far as it can toward the top-right corner.

feedback.default: The bishop only moves diagonally — pick the diagonal heading up and to the right from c1, and go as far as the board allows.

successExplanation: Bh6 travels the whole c1–h6 diagonal in one move — bishops move diagonally, any distance, until something blocks them.

prompt: Move the bishop diagonally down-left as far as possible.

feedback.default: Down-left means the file letter and the rank number both decrease together. From d5, trace that diagonal to the edge of the board.

successExplanation: Ba2 follows the d5–a2 diagonal to the board's edge — every bishop move stays on a single diagonal, and always on the same square colour.

prompt: Move the queen straight across its rank to the right-hand edge of the board.

feedback.default: The queen can move like a rook (straight lines) or a bishop (diagonals). This time, slide it sideways along rank 4, all the way to the right edge.

successExplanation: Qh4 slides along rank 4 to the edge — the queen combines rook and bishop movement, so straight-line moves like this are always available too.

prompt: Move the queen diagonally down-right, all the way to the corner of the board.

feedback.default: This time use the queen's diagonal movement, like a bishop — head down and to the right from d4 until you reach the edge.

successExplanation: Qg1 travels the whole diagonal from d4 down to the corner — the queen's diagonal moves work exactly like a bishop's.

prompt: Move your king one square diagonally, toward the kingside (right).

feedback.default: Picture the eight squares surrounding your king — the kingside diagonal move goes up and to the right. Which square is that?

successExplanation: Kf6 steps one square diagonally — the king can move one square in any of the eight directions, as long as the destination isn't attacked.

prompt: Move your king one square straight up the board.

feedback.default: Straight up means staying on the same file and moving to the next rank. From e1, which square is that?

successExplanation: Ke2 moves straight up one rank — a simple, single-square step, exactly what the king is limited to.

prompt: Move the knight in its L-shape to reach d2.

feedback.default: The knight jumps in an L-shape: two squares in one direction, then one square to the side. From b1, which squares can it reach?

successExplanation: Nd2 is a legal L-shaped jump — two files across and one rank up — and the knight is the only piece that can leap over anything in between.

prompt: Move the knight to a3 instead.

feedback.default: From b1, the knight's L-shape options are a3, c3, and d2. Try the one on the a-file.

successExplanation: Na3 is another valid L-shape from b1 — one square across, two ranks up.

prompt: Push the pawn two squares forward, using its first-move option.

feedback.default: A pawn on its starting square can move one OR two squares straight ahead — but only on its very first move. Which square is two ahead of e2?

successExplanation: e4 uses the pawn's special first-move option — two squares forward instead of the usual one, only available before it has moved.

prompt: Capture the black pawn diagonally in front of you.

feedback.default: Pawns move straight ahead but capture diagonally — one square forward-left or forward-right, only onto a square with an enemy piece. Which diagonal has the black pawn?

successExplanation: exd4 captures diagonally — pawns can only capture on the diagonal squares ahead of them, never straight ahead.

prompt: Castle kingside to get your king to safety.

feedback.default: That's not castling kingside — move your king two squares toward the h-file rook.

successExplanation: O-O gets the king to safety and brings the rook to f1, both in one move.

feedback.default: That's not queenside castling — move your king two squares toward the a-file rook.

successExplanation: O-O-O — the king slides two squares toward the a-file rook, which hops over to d1.
